title: India's Urban Water and Sanitation Crisis
background: India faces severe urban water and sanitation crises causing 25% of global diarrheal deaths and 6.4% GDP loss. Critical infrastructure includes water distribution systems and sanitation facilities.
problem: Indian urban centers lack adequate wastewater treatment, causing groundwater contamination and coastal pollution. Water scarcity worsens with declining per capita renewable freshwater (from 5,177 to 1,588 m³ since 1951). Supply falls short (69 vs 135 lpcd), with intermittent access (2–3 hours). Untreated sewage remains the largest land-based pollution source for coastal areas.
department: Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation
key_outcomes: Reduction in diarrheal deaths (25% of global)
Poorest households suffer 1.75x national economic impact from inadequate sanitation
lessons_learned: Inadequate wastewater treatment leads to groundwater and coastal pollution
Water scarcity worsens due to declining per capita renewable freshwater
Intermittent water access (2-3 hours) affects urban households
